dimensions.reasons: The submitted hero image, .eval_workspace/exports/volcano_dusk.png, clearly depicts a centered active conical volcano at dusk with a summit crater/lava lake, multiple descending lava paths, a large smoke plume, and flank steam features. Group A wide_front.png and wide_high.png confirm these elements are arranged in the intended overall hierarchy.
issues: The cone reads more as a simplified brown mound than a detailed dark basalt-and-ash stratovolcano.
Lava flows and fumaroles are visually artificial enough to weaken the requested geology-illustration fidelity.
The very dark areas of the scene obscure some of the requested layering and terrain information.

dimensions.reasons: The mountain is continuously grounded in the surrounding terrain, the summit opening is structurally integrated with the cone, and the lava paths generally follow the slope in detail_flows.png. The main smoke plume is visibly connected above the summit.
issues: The lava paths read as nearly zero-thickness emissive strips laid on the surface, with sharply cut ends rather than viscous flows with built-up cooling margins.
The summit's front lava segment in detail_crater.png looks like a vertical patterned panel rather than naturally flowing molten material.
Several fumarole volumes have hard, truncated conical or rectangular silhouettes and unclear terrain attachment, especially in detail_fumaroles.png.

dimensions.reasons: The recognizable volcano silhouette, orange emissive lava, dark cracked patterning, brown-gray smoke, and blue-gray dusk sky create a readable warm-versus-cool volcanic scene. The lava lake is especially visible in detail_crater.png.
issues: The rock is predominantly warm brown rather than convincingly dark basalt mixed with volcanic ash.
The lava's repeated bright yellow/orange cellular pattern is graphic and uniform, rather than an orange-red to dark-red melt with irregular black crust.
The small fumaroles do not convincingly read as semi-transparent white steam; they appear as opaque geometric pale-brown forms.

dimensions.reasons: The hero output has a clean render and the primary smoke cloud has some soft volumetric character. Warm lava illumination on nearby slopes is visible in volcano_dusk.png and wide_front.png.
issues: The lava surface pattern repeats strongly across the lake and every flow, making it look like a mapped graphic rather than cooling lava.
The fumaroles are noticeably boxy/tapered objects rather than diffuse turbulent vapor.
Strong shadowing makes much of the east-facing cone nearly unreadable in wide_east.png.
The mountain and surrounding terrain share a similar uniformly granular brown material, reducing natural material variation.

dimensions.reasons: The core spatial arrangement is correct: the cone dominates the center, the crater/lava lake sits at its apex, the smoke rises vertically above it, and lava routes descend separate flanks. wide_high.png also shows steam forms distributed around the slopes and rear of the volcano.
issues: The finished hero composition crops the cone's base at the lower frame edge, limiting clarity of the full base footprint.
Several steam plumes are partially hidden behind the cone or terrain and do not read clearly as slope-based vents.
Deep shadow causes some lava and terrain relationships to disappear from side views.

dimensions.reasons: Across the Group A overview views, the volcano has a sensible broad-base/tall-cone relationship, a relatively small summit opening, narrow lava paths, and a plume taller than the mountain. The lava lake is visibly contained within the summit rim in detail_crater.png.
issues: The summit lava lake appears as a very flat patterned disk and its apparent size varies awkwardly with the rim.
The flank steam columns are oversized and too geometrically regular relative to the mountain surface.
Because the base is cropped in volcano_dusk.png, the requested overall cone-to-base scale is less immediately legible in the hero image.

dimensions.reasons: volcano_dusk.png provides a credible graded blue-gray dusk sky and uses the lava as a warm local source, visibly lighting portions of nearby rock. The cone has a rough displaced/granular surface rather than a plain default material.
issues: The cool fill is too weak on much of the cone, producing broad nearly black regions rather than readable dusk-form shading.
Rock color and texture are too uniformly brown and granular for the requested basalt-plus-ash material distinction.
Lava lacks convincing thick molten body, varied hot-to-cool coloration, and dark cooled crust along its outer edges.

dimensions.reasons: The renders visibly include the required major elements: a stratovolcano-shaped cone, crater opening, lava lake, at least three lava routes, a summit smoke plume, several flank vapor features, surrounding terrain, and a dusk backdrop. The cracked lava treatment is clearly present in detail_crater.png and detail_flows.png.
issues: The requested five-to-six fumaroles are not all clearly identifiable as individual, diffuse steam vents in the final hero view.
Cooled lava crust along flow edges is not convincingly represented.
The lava's requested orange-red through dark-red color range is largely replaced by a bright yellow-orange repeated pattern.

criteria.criterion: The principal landform is a correctly proportioned stratovolcano with the complete specified slope-surface system.
The summit contains the correctly scaled crater-and-lava-lake assembly with the complete specified molten surface treatment.
The repeated lava-flow system has the required count, scale, terrain relationship, and molten-versus-cooled surface construction.
The complete fumarole system has the required vent count, slope distribution, and attached semi-transparent steam.
A distinct large-scale volcanic smoke plume rises above the summit and remains distinguishable from slope steam.
criteria.evidence: The designated hero image, .eval_workspace/exports/volcano_dusk.png, clearly shows a large brown-gray smoke column emerging directly from the summit and broadening into a mushroom-like cloud high above the cone. It is substantially larger and higher than the small pale steam plumes on the slopes.

criteria.criterion: The scene combines genuine lava-cast warm illumination with cool environmental dusk fill.
The final author camera and composition clearly communicate the dusk geothermal subject, central hierarchy, scale, layering, label space, and requested viewpoint.
The delivered Blender project is openable and editable and retains the required Cycles configuration for a clean hero render.
The final image delivery provides one designated hero render at the required actual resolution.

notes: This is a clearly recognizable active dusk volcano scene with the requested central cone, lava lake, descending flows, smoke, and geothermal vents. Its principal weaknesses are the thin patterned-sheet appearance of lava, geometric fumaroles, overly brown uniform terrain, and dark side lighting that limits the intended geological readability.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
